t: No account by a participant survives, and the earliest reports differ so much that the course of the battle cannot be reconstructed with confidence; estimates of the armies run from 15,000 to 20,000 for Lazar and 27,000 to 30,000 for Murad.
Murad I was killed, the only time an Ottoman sultan died in battle, and tradition ascribes his death to the Serbian knight Miloš Obilić, though early accounts differ on who killed him and when.

The Kosovo Myth, built on motifs of sacrifice, betrayal and heroism, grew from oral epic poetry and gained its modern importance in the 19th century, and Vidovdan is now an important Serbian national and religious holiday.
dyk: The battle is the only time in history an Ottoman sultan was killed in battle, yet a Florentine letter of 1389 names no killer, and an Italian work of 1416 says that Lazar killed Murad.
ev: The Ottomans destroy much of the Serbian nobility at the Battle of Maritsa, and Stefan Uroš V dies childless in December
The Ottomans are defeated at Pločnik, and again at Bileća in 1388
Murad I moves his troops from Philippoupolis to Ihtiman and on towards Kosovo
Murad arrives at Pristina on 14 June and Lazar brings his army to the Kosovo field
The battle is fought on 15 June, and Murad and Lazar are both killed
Tvrtko I of Bosnia writes to Trogir and Florence claiming a victory over the Ottomans
The Ottomans renew their campaign in southern Serbia, 1390 to 1391
The capture of Smederevo on 20 June ends medieval Serbian statehood

f.date: 15 June 1389; Vidovdan, the day the battle is commemorated, falls on 28 June in the Gregorian calendar, and a Florentine letter of 20 October 1389 gives 28 June (St Vitus' day)
f.place: The Kosovo field, about 5 kilometres north-west of Pristina, in present-day Kosovo, on land ruled by Vuk Branković
f.sides: The Ottoman Empire under Sultan Murad I, leading estimate 27,000 to 30,000 men, with a higher estimate of 40,000; a coalition under Prince Lazar Hrebeljanović, leading estimate 15,000 to 20,000, with a higher estimate of 25,000. Both figures are disputed.
f.outcome: Lazar and Murad were both killed and most of both armies were lost. Serbian manpower was depleted, and the Serbian principalities that were not already Ottoman vassals became so in the following years.
